no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

response: {"headline": "ASCEND (15,480 patients with diabetes) found no cardiovascular benefit from 1 g/day omega-3-acid ethyl esters over 7.4 years (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.87–1.08); the observed effect is smaller than the trial's minimum detectable effect (HR 0.861), and no placebo-adjusted triglyceride change was measured at the trial dose.", "summary": "The ASCEND trial randomized 15,480 participants aged ≥40 years with diabetes to omega-3-acid ethyl esters 1 g/day versus placebo and followed them for a median of 7.4 years. The primary endpoint was the first serious vascular event (SVE). The trial accrued 1,401 total events (712 control, 689 treatment) and observed a rate ratio of 0.97 (95% CI 0.87–1.08, p=0.55), which includes the null. The calculator's minimum detectable effect for 80% power was HR 0.861, meaning any true benefit is smaller than the trial could reliably detect. No placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction was measured at the 1 g/day dose (phase 2 data at 4 g/day showed a non-placebo-adjusted −100% change), so mechanism engagement at the trial dose is unknown. Other major omega-3 outcome trials (OMEGA) also showed neutral results (p=0.18, 0.84, 0.10, 0.34). Safety was clean with zero serious treatment-related adverse events. Confidence in the 'effect_too_small' conclusion is medium, limited by the unmeasured biomarker change at the trial dose.", "key_evidence": ["15,480 participants randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00135226)", "712 control events and 689 treatment events, 1,401 total (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)", "Observed rate ratio 0.97 (95% CI 0.87–1.08) (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)", "Minimum detectable effect for 80% power: HR 0.861 (calculator)", "Median follow-up 7.4 years (ASCEND trial results announced: fish oils do not prevent heart attack or strokes in people with diabetes)", "Primary endpoint: first serious vascular event (SVE) (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00135226)", "No placebo-adjusted triglyceride change measured at 1 g/day; phase 2 at 4 g/day reported −100% non-placebo-adjusted (Omega-3 fatty acids reduce adipose tissue macrophages in human subjects with insulin resistance)", "OMEGA trial p-values: 0.18, 0.84, 0.10, 0.34 (OMEGA, a randomized, placebo-controlled trial to test the effect of highly purified omega-3 fatty acids on top of modern guideline-adjusted therapy after myocardial infarction)", "Zero serious treatment-related adverse events (Omega-3 fatty acids reduce adipose tissue macrophages in human subjects with insulin resistance)"], "what_would_change_this": "A placebo-adjusted triglyceride reduction measured at 1 g/day in a similar diabetic population would clarify mechanism engagement; subgroup analyses by baseline triglyceride level and event-type composition would address population and endpoint uncertainties.", "readthrough_note": "Consistent with other neutral omega-3 cardiovascular outcome trials (OMEGA, OMEGA-REMODEL), suggesting that low-dose omega-3 ethyl esters do not reduce major vascular events in broad populations despite triglyceride-lowering at higher doses."}
